Given that the slope of the line shown above is $-3,$ the equation of the line is $y=${{field-1}}
$x\,-$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ We know that the slope is $m=-3,$ so we just need to work out $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,-2).$ So, the $y$-intercept is $b=-2.$

Substituting the slope $m=-3$ and the $y$-intercept $b=-2$ into the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b,$ we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
y=-3x-2
$$
